transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, my wife wanted me to come in. She says I’m not eating enough. I don’t really see it that way, but most days I just have coffee and toast in the morning, and maybe some soup or vegetables later on. Big meals just feel unnecessary at my age.
Do you think you are underweight?

No, I don’t really think so. I mean, maybe I’m thinner than I used to be, but I don’t see why everyone’s making such a fuss. Older folks don’t need to eat as much, and I’m still getting my chores done and going on my tours, so I feel like I’m managing fine.
Are you trying to lose weight?

I wouldn’t say I’m trying to lose weight exactly. But when my wife puts butter on things or gives me a big full plate, I do get nervous. I feel like I’ll start putting weight back on, and I don’t want to lose the control I’ve managed to keep.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes… I suppose I am, at least some. When my wife puts butter on things or gives me a full plate, I get nervous I’ll start putting weight back on. I don’t like that feeling, like I’m losing the control I’ve been trying to keep.
Do you think you would be happier if you were thinner?

I don’t know if “happier” is the word, but… I do feel better about myself when my belt feels a notch looser, like I’ve done something right. If I look in the mirror and my stomach seems even a little rounded, I feel sloppy and disappointed in myself.
Do you think you look fat even when others say you're thin?

Yes… I guess I do sometimes. Other people may say I’m thin, but if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even a little rounded, I feel sloppy, like I’ve let myself go. And if my belt is a notch looser, I feel like I’ve done something right.
Do you feel like eating a normal amount would make you lose control over your weight?

Yes. If I eat what other people would call a normal amount, especially if my wife gives me a full plate or adds butter, I start worrying I’ll put weight back on. It feels like I’d be letting go of the control I’ve been trying to keep.
Do you feel like you would be unable to stop eating once you start if you allowed yourself to eat a normal amount?

I’m not sure. I don’t usually think of it as not being able to stop once I start. It’s more that the idea of eating a normal amount makes me uneasy. But I haven’t really noticed myself losing control like that.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past few months?

Yes, I have lost some weight. My doctor says the number on the scale has gotten too low. I don’t really see it that way, though… being lighter makes it easier for me to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Do you fear eating because you think you won't be able to control how much you eat once you start?
Not really in that sense. I don’t usually feel like I’d start eating and then not be able to stop. It’s more just that eating more than I’m used to makes me uncomfortable.
Do you feel anxious or upset when you think about eating or gaining weight?

Yes… I do get anxious about gaining weight. Like when my wife puts butter on things or gives me a full plate, I get nervous that I’ll start putting weight back on and lose the control I’ve been trying to keep.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the most important aspect of your self-evaluation?

I suppose it matters more than I’d like to admit. If my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I’ve done right by myself. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach seems even a little rounded, I feel sloppy… disappointed in myself.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because you believe it would change your appearance in a way that you couldn't accept?

Yes, I think that’s part of it. If my belt feels a little looser, I feel like I’m doing okay. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even a bit rounded, I feel sloppy… disappointed in myself.
Do you think your eating habits are aimed at preventing a loss of control over how much you eat?

Yes, I think so. I try to keep things limited because I worry if I start eating more—like when my wife gives me a full plate or puts butter on something—I’ll put weight back on and lose the control I’ve been trying to hold onto.
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if you couldn't see your body?

Yes… I think I would. Even if I couldn’t see myself, I’d still worry about gaining weight. Like when my wife puts butter on food or gives me a full plate, I get nervous that I’ll start putting weight back on and lose the control I’ve been trying to keep.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is mostly about how you think you look to others?

Maybe a little, but mostly it’s how I see myself. If my belt feels looser, I feel like I’ve done something right. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even a little rounded, I feel sloppy… and disappointed in myself.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about not wanting to look a certain way?

Yes, mostly. It’s about not wanting my body to look a certain way. If my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I’ve done right by myself. But if I see my stomach looking even a little rounded in the mirror, I feel sloppy… disappointed in myself.
Do you think your weight is lower than a normal weight for someone of your age and height?

My doctor says the number on the scale has gotten too low. I hear that, but… to me, being lighter feels easier. I can get around the garden better and keep up with my walks, so it doesn’t feel too low to me the same way it does to him.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because you have a distorted view of what you actually look like?

I suppose it could be. I don’t always see what other people say they see. I just know that when my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I’ve done right by myself. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even a little rounded, I feel sloppy and disappointed.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about feeling like you'd lose control over your eating or your body if you were to gain weight?

Yes… I think that’s part of it. When my wife puts butter on things or gives me a full plate, I get nervous. It feels like if I start eating that way, I’ll put the weight back on and lose the control I’ve worked hard to keep.
